title: Interrequest context compactors and GPU residence orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our current GPU-resident KV store keeps many near-duplicate context fragments from interleaved requests, which increases resident memory, worsens slab fragmentation, and raises tail latency for hot tenants. This ticket designs and implements a compacting layer (Context Compactor) plus a GPU Residence Orchestrator that together: (1) identify semantically overlapping prompt fragments across requests, (2) consolidate and store canonical microfragments to reduce duplicate KV slots, and (3) schedule residency/eviction of fragments with a reuse-aware planner that respects tenant isolation and latency SLOs. Goals: 1) Reduce GPU KV residency by 20-35% for mixed PLG/enterprise workloads. 2) Reduce 95th tail latency for small single-token continuations by 8-12% for workloads with high prompt overlap. 3) Keep per-tenant isolation guarantees (no cross-tenant leakage) and support fast rollbacks.
technical_acceptance_criteria: Context Compactor will produce canonical fragment ids and mapping tables for >=99% of exact duplicates and cluster semantically similar fragments at >=80% precision in our offline evals.
GPU Residence Orchestrator will integrate with the slab allocator and enforce per-tenant residency budgets; memory usage reduction measurable end-to-end on staging.gpu cluster.
No regressions on single-request latency for cold-starts (>1% P50, >3% P95).
Automated simulation harness and microbenchmarks added to CI; PRs include results and configuration for 3 representative workloads (chat, completion-heavy, retrieval-augmented prompts).
implementation_notes: Approach: 1) Fingerprint fragments with a short stable hash + 64-bit locality-preserving sketch (murmur3 + simhash variant) to detect exact and near duplicates. 2) Maintain a lightweight Fragment Registry (metadata only) in host memory; canonical microfragments are materialized into GPU slabs on first compact-write. 3) Merge-on-access policy: when two fragments are highly similar (above threshold) they are stored once and a delta pointer reconstructed at decode time for context expansion. 4) GPU Residence Orchestrator computes a reuse score = alpha * recent_hits + beta * expected_future_reuse - gamma * residency_cost, using periodic telemetry from batching layer. 5) Eviction uses slab-aware coalescing to avoid leaving tiny gaps; we schedule proactive prefetch for fragments likely to be reused in the next N requests. Trade-offs: merge-on-access saves memory but adds a small CPU/GPU reconstruction cost; thresholds will be tuned per-model/sequence-length.
implementation_plan: Spike: build offline cluster simulator to replay request traces and validate compaction heuristics (2w).
Phase 1: implement fingerprinting + Fragment Registry + exact-duplicate compaction (3w).
Phase 2: integrate with slab allocator + GPU Residence Orchestrator, add reuse scoring and eviction policies (3w).
Phase 3: near-duplicate clustering + merge-on-access, add prefetching hooks in continuous-batching path (3w).
Phase 4: rollout canary on staging/dedicated small pool, collect telemetry and iterate thresholds (2w).
benchmarks_and_targets: Memory: 20-35% resident KV reduction on mixed workloads (chat + completions).
Latency: 8-12% P95 improvement for short continuation requests in overlapping workloads.
Cost: reduce tokens-served GPU-hours by ~10% at 99th percentile load due to better residency efficiency.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False merges could degrade output quality. Mitigation: conservative similarity threshold, QA evals on held-out prompts, and an automatic rollback flag tied to quality regressions.

Risk: Increased CPU overhead for reconstruction. Mitigation: measure CPU tail and optionally offload delta reconstruction to a dedicated worker queue or perform lightweight in-GPU recomposition kernels.
Risk: Tenant isolation bugs. Mitigation: design registry keys with tenant-scoped namespaces and run fuzz tests to ensure no cross-tenant references.
